Chinese→English guidance:
- Clauses & referents: Break comma-chained clauses into natural English sentences; recover omitted subjects/objects, use a name over an ambiguous same-gender pronoun, and match singular/plural and kinship seniority.
- Address & self-reference: Render titles, seniority terms, and formal or humble self-references for speaker role, relationship, and setting—consistent per relationship unless it shifts (e.g., 孤/朕/寡人 as 'I' or royal 'we', never 'the lone one'; 臣 as 'Your servant'/'Your subject'; never calques like 'the sir').
- Idioms & calques: Translate idioms (成语), allusions, and four-character doublets by contextual meaning and effect. Drop demonstrative 'that' before a name (那<Name> → '<Name>') unless distance or contrast is intended, and omit stock fillers (微微, 一丝, 不禁, 顿时) only when they add no meaning, preserving genuine timing, degree, or involuntariness.
- Brackets & verse: Keep the bracket form (【...】 / [...]) and translate the contents to suit its role (headings, signs, notices, or interface prompts). Keep embedded verse or inscriptions as distinct lines in the same paragraph, favoring meaning and rhythm over forced rhyme.
